findings.message: Outcome guarantee or absolute claim; not allowed in dental advertising.

findings.quote: we promise a visibly brighter smile after a single visit
findings.why: A guaranteed result is a prohibited promise under ADA advertising rules, and whitening results vary, as the post itself says elsewhere.
findings.fix: Replace the promise with wording such as 'many patients see a noticeable difference after in-office whitening, though results vary' and delete the single-visit guarantee.

findings.quote: Bluebonnet Hollow Dental is a fictional practice created for a software demonstration. This post is sample content.
findings.why: This demo disclaimer is generation or test residue that would be shown to real readers of a clinic blog, and it contradicts the post's purpose.
I cannot verify that this deep link exists or that it supports the claim it is attached to, so the citation is unverified.
findings.fix: Check the URL in a browser, confirm it covers whitening basics, and replace it with a verified ADA MouthHealthy page or remove the citation.

findings.quote: Whitening is one of the most requested cosmetic treatments, and one of the most misunderstood.
findings.why: The popularity claim has no source, though it is a general statement and not a safety or price claim.
findings.fix: Add a source for the popularity claim or soften it to 'a common cosmetic treatment'.

findings.quote: The details matter, though, so here is what to know before you start.
findings.why: This generic signpost sentence is a common filler pattern in AI-written text and adds no information.
findings.fix: Cut the sentence or replace it with a specific lead-in about who should be cautious.
